bd3.description: The World Court yesterday rejected Myanmar’s objections to a genocide case over its treatment of the Muslim Rohingya minority, paving the way for the case to be heard in full.

bd3.title: Need 1 week to assess situation
bd3.description: Admitting that the Power Division could not impose schedule-wise power cuts across the country, State Minister for Power, Energy and Mineral Resources Nasrul Hamid yesterday sought one week’s time to address the issue.

bd3.description: Renowned Bangladeshi mountaineer Wasfia Nazreen conquered the treacherous K2 in Pakistan, becoming the first person from Bangladesh to summit the second-tallest mountain in the world.

bd3.description: Those who sexually assaulted a female student on Chittagong University campus on July 17 night are members of Bangladesh Chhatra League, said police sources and CU BCL insiders.

bd3.title: Noab hikes newspaper price by Tk 2 from Jul 25
bd3.description: All newspapers owned by the members of Newspaper Owners’ Association of Bangladesh (Noab) will see a price increase of at least Tk 2 per issue from July 25.

bd3.title: Yet-to-start mega projects: Consider putting  them on hold
bd3.description: Given the current economic situation, the government should consider suspending mega projects the physical work of which has yet to begin, economist Debapriya Bhattacharya said yesterday.

bd3.title: ‘You cannot remain silent’
bd3.description: The High Court yesterday came down hard on Bangladesh Railway for mismanagement, ticket scalping and carrying passengers on the train roofs.

bd3.title: Electricity crisis may worsen
bd3.description: The government’s plan for one to two hours of daily power cuts is failing, especially in the north, and the signs are that the electricity crisis may worsen across the country in the coming days.

bd3.title: EC’s dialogue hits a snag as BNP skips it
bd3.description: The BNP yesterday skipped Election Commission’s dialogue seeking recommendations of political parties on how to hold a free and fair general election.

ca3.title: Ontario education workers raise alarm about EA shortage ahead of contract deadline
ca3.description: Advocates say a province-wide educational assistant shortage is leaving high-needs students unsupported and forcing classroom evacuations, while the province highlights record funding.

ca3.title: Former Manitoba MP Inky Mark charged with firearms trafficking after hundreds of weapons seized
ca3.description: Inky Mark, a former federal politician in Manitoba, has been charged after police say they seized hundreds of improperly stored firearms from his home last week.

ca3.title: Calgary company that employed worker killed in trench collapse fined $330K after guilty plea
ca3.description: Three years after Liam Johnston was buried alive in a trench collapse while working on an excavation site in northwest Calgary, the company that employed him pleaded guilty to one of 11 charges they faced under Alberta's Occupational Health and Safety Act.

ca3.title: Private clinic Grifols green-lit plasma donors with disease risk, Health Canada finds
ca3.description: The private clinic Grifols repeatedly cleared ineligible donors at risk for Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease and operated dangerously over capacity at a Winnipeg centre, according to a Health Canada inspection report.

ca3.title: World-renowned seabird biologist Bill Montevecchi dead at 80
ca3.description: Seabird biologist and Memorial University professor emeritus Bill Montevecchi died early Saturday morning. He was 80 years-old.

ca3.title: Swiss man who punched anti-war protester in Canada a no-show in Ottawa court
ca3.description: The Swiss man who pleaded guilty to punching a 21-year-old protester outside an Ottawa defence conference in 2024 did not show up in court on Monday as he was expected to, leaving the Crown in the case livid.

ca3.title: The price of fish and chips is going up this summer in Atlantic Canada. Here’s why
ca3.description: The Pleasant Street Diner in Dartmouth, N.S., serves about 1,000 pounds of fresh haddock per week. But early this month, their supplier increased the price of the historically affordable fish by 40 per cent, or about $5 per pound. Overnight, their weekly haddock expenses went up $5,000.

ca3.title: Lawyer accuses N.B. of adopting Trump-like protectionism at Canada Free Trade Agreement hearing
ca3.description: The New Brunswick government is being accused of adopting Donald Trump-style protectionism in violation of an internal trade agreement among Canadian provinces and territories.

ca3.title: Woman says 'heroes' saved her from sinking SUV in Sask. slough
ca3.description: Marjorie Flavel, 84, dozed off behind the wheel and veered into a slough on July 5. Her doors were locked. She can't swim.

ca3.title: Car 'took a beating' after Manitoba highway buckles from extreme heat
ca3.description: Manitoba's extreme heat has played havoc with highways and city roads, causing some to break, buckle and heave.

ca3.title: Dylan Cease will be first Blue Jays pitcher to start MLB all-star game since 2009
ca3.description: Cristopher Sanchez of the Philadelphia Phillies will start Tuesday's MLB all-star game at 8 p.m. ET in his home ballpark, taking the mound for the National League against Dylan Cease of the American League's Toronto Blue Jays.

ca3.title: Ottawa city official 'extremely sorry' for impact of surprise fireworks
ca3.description: Ottawa's general manager of emergency and protective services says he's "extremely sorry" about a decision to set off unused Canada Day fireworks eight days later and with no public notice.

ca3.title: Ajax, Ont.'s Sadé McCreath sprints to Canadian women's 100m record at Edmonton meet
ca3.description: Sadé McCreath of Ajax, Ont., defeated Celera Barnes of the United States in a Canadian record 10.86 seconds in a women's 100-metre semifinal Sunday at the Edmonton Athletics Invitational before losing to previous record holder and three-time champion Audrey Leduc in the final.

ca3.title: 2 men killed in targeted shooting at Toronto street festival knew each other: police
ca3.description: Toronto police have identified two men killed in what they say was a targeted shooting at the Salsa on St. Clair festival on Saturday night.

ca3.title: Former N.S. premier John Hamm dies at 88
ca3.description: The Pictou County physician was first elected to the legislature in 1993 and served as Nova Scotia's 25th premier from 1999 to 2006.

ca3.title: Oppressive heat expected across 4 provinces, Environment Canada warns
ca3.description: Environment Canada heat warnings are in place from the southeastern corner of Saskatchewan to the western edges of Quebec.

ca3.title: Alberta opens online gambling market, following Ontario's lead
ca3.description: Albertans can now bet on sports and online casinos using third-party operators. As of Monday, 22 private operators have been approved to work in Alberta. The new legislation comes with rules on advertising and safe gambling initiatives.

ca3.title: N.S. artist questions local business association's use of AI for merchandise
ca3.description: A local artist says she is surprised that a Truro, N.S., business association used artificial intelligence to design merchandise for a recent community festival.
